subject: maths
question: A can do a piece of work in 15 days working 6 hours per day and B can do it in 10 days working 5 hours per day. How long (in days) will they take to do it, working together for 9 hours per day?
solution:
Given:

A can do a piece of work in 15 days working 6 hours per day and B can do it in 10 days working 5 hours per day. 

Concept used:

Total work = Efficiency of worker × Number of Hours × Number of days to finish

Calculation:

Let the efficiencies of A and B be M and N respectively.

Total work = 15 × 6 × M = 90M (Considering A's perspective)

According to the concept,

15 × 6 × M = 10 × 5 × N

⇒ 9M = 5N

⇒ N = 1.8M

Now, the time taken to complete the work by A and B working together for 9 hours per day

⇒ 90M ÷ 9(M + N)

⇒ 10M ÷ (M + 1.8M)

⇒ 10M ÷ 2.8M

⇒ 3 (4)/(7) days

**∴ Working together for 9 hours per day A and B will take 3 (4)/(7) days to complete the work.**
